label: Game B
nuance_found: Real but light. Your own painted ground heals you and slows the ink, so you fight from colour you made. Chain kills build a multiplier, and BLOOM is a charge you hold for a crowd. After the first inkwell you pick a lens (Rapid or Arc, where a kill leaps to the next ink). Dying costs a little score, not the run. I used these but never found a case where the obvious move (hold FIRE, sweep the crowd, bloom when charged) was wrong, and I only had one lens choice in nine minutes.
audio: A looping decoded-audio music bed the whole time, plus dense layered chimes, pops and sweeps on every kill and chain callout, a falling sawtooth on hits taken, and a lens-pick sting; effects were busy and satisfying.
furthest_progress: Olive Terraces inkwell cleared (3 nodes broken, lantern lit, 'restored'), chose Arc lens, then Millbrook: wave-cleared node 1 and node 2 of its inkwell, not finished. 5.2% restored, score about 76,000 at x5 chain, 4 inkwells left (Millbrook, Vell Market, Windmill Ridge, Chalk Quarry).
control_trouble: Aiming with a drag on the right side and walking with the stick were slow for my 0.5 s look rate, so I over-turned and lost crowds several times, and the 'ink took you' deaths in Millbrook are partly me not seeing a wide enemy to dash away from. A real thumb would aim faster, though the camera did clip through house walls and a stone arch.
best_moment: Holding fire into a crowd of ink blobs while the ground blooms into colour and the multiplier climbs to BRILLIANT x3, then the whole terrace lights up and 'The lantern is lit'.
worst_moment: After a death you wake back at the lantern a long walk from the inkwell, and the walk back across a quiet field was dead time.
verdict: This one actually feels like a finished game: the ink-to-colour reveal is a strong hook and every kill pays off in sound, number and a ground that changes. It is a shooter with a good wrapper, though. Hold fire, kite, chain, bloom, and the lens pick at the end of a level is the first real decision, only once so far. The nodes gating each inkwell and the paint-heals-you rule give it a little texture, but by minute three I was playing the same way as minute one. I would keep it a few more sessions for the look and feel, but I would not tell friends about it yet.
